concerns.text: Task T021 describes a mathematically invalid data flow: 'Computing the weighted mean/variance of elemental properties using the CLR-transformed composition values as weights'. This violates the producer-consumer dependency for valid feature engineering. The spec (FR-014) and plan require CLR transformation to map compositions to Euclidean space, but using the transformed values as *weights* for raw properties is semantically incorrect and will produce invalid artifacts. The task order implies a dependency on a flawed transformation logic that must be corrected before T022 (VIF) or T023 (Training) can consume the output.

Task T047 ('Implement explicit data source fallback logic') is ordered in Phase N (Polish) but describes a core dependency for T012 (Aggregator). T012 explicitly states: 'If a specific source fails, aggregate whatever partial data was successfully retrieved...'. T047 duplicates this logic. If T012 is implemented without T047, the pipeline may crash on a single source failure, violating the data-flow requirement to produce partial data. T047 must be moved to Phase 3 (US1) to ensure the producer (T012) is robust before any consumer (T013-T017) runs.

Task T049 ('Ensure descriptor_engine.py handles N < 50') is placed in Phase N (Polish) but is a hard dependency for T023 (Model Training). The spec (US1 Edge Cases) requires the system to halt or warn if N < 50. If T023 runs before T049 is implemented, the model training will proceed on statistically invalid data, producing garbage artifacts. The validation logic (T049) must precede the consumer (T023) in the execution order.

Task T005 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly states 'depends on T007 for model imports'. While T005 and T007 are in the same phase, the explicit dependency note contradicts the [P] tag which implies no ordering requirement. This is a semantic ordering violation; T005 cannot run in parallel with T007 if it imports from it. The tag should be removed or the dependency clarified.
